rationale: I read the complete held EO 11098 (28 FR 2615, Mar. 19, 1963): prescribes amendments to the Selective Service Regulations (32 CFR ch. XVI, parts 1621, 1622, 1625, 1626, 1628 and others) made by earlier EOs 10001 ff.; no own term or sunset (the 'until' and 'fixed term' machine hits are regulation text about registrants, not a limit on the order). I read the held EO 12553 (51 FR 7237 ff., Mar. 3, 1986, 'Revocation of Various Executive Orders'): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked', followed by the No./Subject table, whose row reads '11098 Amending Selective Service regulations' (matching the title 'Amending the Selective Service Regulations' of EO 11098). The order is dated Feb. 25, 1986 and has no savings clause and no exceptions. The dossier does not locate this provision as an ACT record, so the basis is the held actor text, which I read against the table myself; the OCR rows are consistent with the printed number/subject pairing. Because it revokes the order 'and any amendments thereto', the later amending orders (EO 11119, 11188, 11241, 11266, 11350, 11360, 11391, 11497, 11527, 11537, 11553, 11563, 11569, 11586, 11606, 1963-1971) are swept in too. Earlier endings: none found. D6 (later events): every history event after EO 11098 is an amendment between Sept. 1963 and 1971, all before the Feb. 1986 revocation; nothing later amends, revives or re-delegates it, and I found no held order naming EO 11098 after 1986. Caveat stated openly: revoking an amending order does not by itself repeal the regulation text it inserted in the CFR; this proposal concerns the executive order instrument only. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
